front: In what order does Python check the conditions of an `if-elif` chain, and how many blocks can run?
back: From top to bottom. It runs the block of the first true condition and then leaves the whole chain, so at most one block runs.
`score >= 90` is false, `score >= 70` is true, so `"B"` is printed. The `else` is skipped because a branch already matched.

front: What does this print, and what is wrong with the order?
back: The first condition `age > 12` is true for 20, so `"teen"` is printed. The later branch `age > 17` can never run because it is a stricter case of a test above it: put the most specific condition first.

front: What happens when no condition in an `if-elif` chain without `else` is true?
back: No branch runs and Python simply continues with the first line after the chain. Only an `else` guarantees that one branch always runs.
`day` is `"Sun"`, which matches neither test, so the fallback `else` branch runs.
